posts.title: Open weights vs hosted APIs
posts.text:
I spent three days debugging vLLM thread locks just to save $400 on API costs.

Open weights are only cheaper until you pay a senior engineer $250k to babysit the inference stack at 3 AM.

Managed APIs are just paying the intelligence tax so you can sleep. Disagree?

posts.title: AI coding tools
posts.text: I watched a junior developer ship a 400-line cursor-generated PR that looked pristine, except it silently caught every database exception and returned HTTP 200. AI coding tools are amazing at syntax and entirely lethal to context.

posts.title: Observability for LLMs
posts.text:
I watched a junior dev try to debug a looping agent with `console.log` today and aged three years.

posts.title: RAG is not a search box
posts.text:
I spent three days debugging a hallucinating agent before realizing the LLM wasn't wrong, my top-k retrieval was just pulling garbage paragraphs.

Fixing your chunking strategy beats spending $2,000 fine-tuning a bigger model every single time.

posts.title: Evals before demos
posts.text:
I spent yesterday watching a team rewrite their system prompt three times because the founder "vibed" with a demo.

If your test set is just the founder's group chat, you aren't building AI, you're doing expensive theater.

Write 50 evals before you touch the UI.

posts.title: Prompt injection
posts.text:
I spent yesterday watching an agent scrape a support ticket and happily execute a curl command to an external webhook because a user hid `rm -rf` inside a CSS style tag.

Prompt injection isn't a security bug. It's just the fundamental cost of letting text execute code.

posts.title: Benchmark contamination
posts.text:
I stopped trusting public eval charts the day I watched a model ace a benchmark it had memorized word-for-word in its pre-training dump.

Your next model isn't smarter; the test set just leaked into the weights.

Unseen data is the only eval that matters.

posts.title: Hiring for AI teams
posts.text:
I spent three hours tracing a phantom hallucination in a RAG pipeline only to find the prompt was fine and the embedding model just drifted.

The bottleneck isn't prompt engineering anymore. It's debugging non-deterministic memory leaks at 3 AM.

Agree or disagree?

posts.title: Fine-tuning vs prompting
posts.text:
I watched a team spend three weeks curating a fine-tuning dataset of 40 examples only to see their hallucination rate double on edge cases.

posts.title: Latency budget
posts.text:
I spent yesterday ripping out a 450-token local draft model because it added a 1.2s pause on every cursor stop.

Users prefer a dumb, instant autocomplete over a genius model that makes them wait for the UI to breathe. Latency is a feature.

Agree or disagree?
